30960.etyen:
The verb is inherited from Old Norse koma (“to come”), from Proto-Germanic *kwemaną (“to come”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷem- (“to come, go”). The noun is a substantivization of the verb.
Cognate with Norwegian Nynorsk koma and komme, Danish komme, Swedish komma, Icelandic koma, Faroese koma, English come, West Frisian komme, Dutch komen, German kommen and Gothic 𐌵𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌽 (qiman, “to come”). More distantly, compare Latin veniō (“I come”) and Ancient Greek βαίνω (baínō, “I walk, go”).

First attested in 1920, when the former municipality was established, as a new name for the settlement previously called Orkedalsøren, also written Orkdalsøren and, in modernized form, Orkdalsøra; locally it was known as Øra. Coined from Ork-, the first element of Orkla and Orkdal, and -anger, from Old Norse angr (“inlet, bay, fjord”). The river-name element is reconstructed as Old Norse *Ork and has traditionally been connected with orka (“to work, labour”), perhaps in reference to the river's strong current, but this interpretation is uncertain.
Compare Orkland, formed from the same river-na

x: Hun tok på seg joggedressen før hun gikk ut.
She put on her tracksuit before going out.
den såkalte joggedressen er kommet på moten
the so-called tracksuit has come into fashion

1004272.etyen:
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from jog (“to jog”) + dress (“clothing, attire”). The formation corresponds to Norwegian jogge (“to jog”) + dress (“suit; leisure or sports outfit”), literally “jogging outfit”. Both elements are ultimately from English.
The first element is from English jog, of uncertain further origin. The second element ultimately belongs to the etymological family of English dress, from Middle English dressen, through Old French dresser, and is ultimately related to Latin regō (“to rule, guide”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃reǵ- (“to straighten, direct”).

x: Kua bruker mange timer om dagen på drøvtygging.

en.g: rehashing; repeated reconsideration, discussion or repetition of a subject, argument or idea, especially one already dealt with
x: Det ble mye drøvtygging av de samme gamle argumentene.
There was a lot of rehashing of the same old arguments.
Han mener altså at det bunadskledde angrepet på Frp er drøvtygging av SV.
He therefore regards the bunad-clad attack on the Progress Party as SV rehashing old material.

1005040.etyen:
From drøvtygge (“to ruminate, chew the cud; to rehash”) + -ing (“action/result-forming noun suffix”). The base verb is a compound of drøv (“cud”) and tygge (“to chew”), literally “to chew cud”; its second element is ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁- (“to chew”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk drøvtygging (“rumination”).
